title: Introduce tenant canary migrator, downgrade-sim harness, and preflight state-checker
author: Leila Mendoza
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need low-risk upgrade paths for multi-tenant clusters. Existing tooling focuses on global dry-runs and snapshot-based rollbacks; this PR adds a lightweight tenant-canary migrator that runs a staged schema/apply workflow against a small tenant slice, a downgrade-simulation harness to validate backwards compatibility of migrations, and a Terraform preflight state-consistency checker that prevents plan application if remote state drift is detected.

Summary of changes: Adds a new operator component (tenant-canary-migrator) that can be configured via Helm to select tenant namespaces by label and execute a two-phase migration: (1) apply compatibility shims and non-breaking changes; (2) run a canary migration job with validation probes; only after canary success will the controller promote to bulk rollout. Introduces downgrade-sim.sh (e2e harness) that replays migration steps against a snapshot of production data in a fenced test namespace to verify downgrade safety. Adds terraform/state-checker module to fail early on unexpected remote state modifications (useful for airgapped installs where state drift is a common source of failed upgrades). Includes docs/upgrade-playbook.md describing runbooks and operator flags.

Design notes: - Tenant canary selection: controller supports two selectors: label-based inclusion and percentage fence. The operator patches the HelmRelease CR (or equivalent) to deploy a migration JobTemplate and waits for user-defined validation probes (HTTP, DB smoke tests, and Redwood-specific evals). - Two-phase apply: compatibility shims (feature flags + compatibility-configmap) are applied first so runtime can tolerate partial schema changes. - Downgrade sim: the harness spins up a quarantined namespace, restores a compressed snapshot, runs the migration forward, then attempts an instrumented downgrade and checks for data integrity and invariant violations. Output is a standardized report consumed by the console. - Terraform preflight: checks provider versions, last-apply commit id in state metadata, and detects suspicious manual resource changes; it fails with actionable messages.

Rollout plan: shipped behind Helm flag values.migration.canary.enabled=false by default. Staged rollout: enable canary on a single cluster in canary region -> 48h observation -> enable on 10% tenant slices -> bulk. Operators default to dry-run for first 24h per cluster to gather telemetry.

Testing: unit tests for controller reconciliation (operator/migrator_test.go), integration that runs downgrade-sim in CI (makes use of mock snapshots), and terraform module tests using tfenv in CI matrix. e2e uses a new lightweight snapshot fixture.

Checklist:
- [x] Add operator and controller logic with reconciliation loop
- [x] Helm values and templating for optional activation and RBAC scopes
- [x] Terraform preflight module and docs
- [x] Downgrade simulation harness and e2e test
- [x] Console report schema and a simple JSON consumer

Commits summary: - "operator: add tenant canary controller with two-phase flow" (migrator.go, reconciler) - "helm: values and templates for canary migrator and job templates" (helm/templates/migration-job.yaml, values.yaml) - "terraform: add state-consistency preflight module" (terraform/modules/state-checker/main.tf) - "e2e: add downgrade-sim harness and fixtures" (test/e2e/downgrade-sim.sh) - "docs: publish upgrade-playbook and troubleshooting notes" (docs/upgrade-playbook.md)

Changed files (high level): - operator/migrator.go - operator/migrator_test.go - helm/values.yaml - helm/templates/migration-job.yaml - terraform/modules/state-checker/main.tf - terraform/modules/state-checker/README.md - test/e2e/downgrade-sim.sh - docs/upgrade-playbook.md - console/reporting/migration-report-schema.json

Small illustrative snippet (helm/templates/migration-job.yaml): "apiVersion: batch/v1\nkind: Job\nmetadata:\n  name: {{ include \"fullname\" . }}-migration-canary\nspec:\n  template:\n    spec:\n      containers:\n      - name: migrator\n        image: {{ .Values.migration.image }}\n        args: [\"--run-canary\", \"--validation-probes={{ .Values.migration.probes }}\"]"

Backwards compatibility: operator gracefully no-ops if migration CRs are absent and all new resources are behind feature flags. Terraform module is additive and returns non-zero exit codes only when inconsistencies are found.

Release notes: "Add tenant canary migrator, downgrade simulation harness, and terraform preflight state checks to reduce upgrade blast radius for private deployments."

review_comments: Connor Blake (reviewer): Can we make the canary selector deterministic across controller restarts? The label+percentage approach may flip tenants if the controller is rescheduled. Suggested: derive a stable hash from tenant namespace and a cluster salt.
Leila Mendoza (author): Thanks, Connor. Implemented stable-hash selection (see operator/migrator.go commit a1f4b2c). Added a cluster-salt Helm value and unit tests that exercise restart scenarios.
Sofia Ramesh (reviewer): Terraform state-checker is very helpful. Two asks: clearer error codes for API retries, and a short circuit mode that only emits warnings in dry-run clusters.
Leila Mendoza (author): Added retry classification and --warn-only flag to the module per Sofia's suggestion. Documented behavior in terraform/modules/state-checker/README.md.
Ethan Wu (reviewer): Downgrade simulation is great. We should gate execution in CI to a separate workflow because it needs snapshot fixtures and can be flaky in shared runners.
Leila Mendoza (author): Split the e2e into a dedicated workflow (migration-downgrade-sim.yml). CI now toggles using an image-based fixture to reduce flakiness.
ci_checks: e2e-downgrade-sim: pass (job run in dedicated workflow)
